Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

charts.title: Distributable Income vs Net Income
charts.annotation: Distributable income, not net income, is the basis for DPU -- it excludes non-cash fair-value gains/losses on investment properties.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR): equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

occupancy.title: Occupancy
occupancy.content:
The share of lettable space (or units) that is leased.

For CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR): occupancy below the sector norm is the first sign of rental pressure.

What to watch:

  • Occupancy trend
  • Lease expiries in the next two years

npi.title: Net property income and NPI margin
npi.content:
Net property income (NPI) is rental and related revenue less property operating expenses (property tax, maintenance, management fees); NPI margin is NPI as a percentage of revenue. This is the REIT equivalent of gross profit/margin -- the line distributable income is built from, before interest, trust expenses and manager's fees.

For CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR): NPI margin has held in a narrow ~69-70% band through FY2022-FY2025 even as the portfolio grew, which says cost pass-throughs and master-lease structures are protecting the margin.

What to watch:

  • NPI margin compression from rising property expenses or utilities costs tenants don't fully bear
  • NPI growth driven by new acquisitions vs same-property rental reversions

distributableIncome.title: Distributable income vs net income
distributableIncome.content:
Distributable income is the cash amount available for unitholder distributions, derived from net income with non-cash items (fair-value gains/losses on investment properties, deferred tax, straight-lining adjustments) added back or stripped out. It is the actual numerator behind DPU, not statutory net income.

For CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR): FY2025 net income of S$769.7m includes revaluation gains that distributable income (S$678.3m) excludes -- using net income alone overstates the cash the REIT can actually pay out.

What to watch:

  • Distributable income growing in line with (or ahead of) unit count, not just in absolute terms
  • Gap between net income and distributable income widening -- a sign revaluations are driving the headline number

costOfDebt.title: Cost of debt
costOfDebt.content:
The weighted average interest rate on the REIT's total borrowings.

For CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR): cost of debt rose from 2.2% (FY2021) to a peak of 3.7% (FY2024) as low-rate borrowings rolled over into the higher-rate environment, before easing to 3.5% in FY2025 -- a direct drag on distributable income that isn't visible in Gearing alone.

What to watch:

  • Cost of debt trend against the REIT's hedged/fixed-rate proportion of borrowings
  • Near-term refinancing maturities at rates above the current weighted average

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
